newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Chirac suggests African force in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac suggests African force in Zaire.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac suggested on Tuesday that a proposed multinational force to ensure security for refugees in eastern Zaire could later be replaced by an African force.

He told a news conference at a Franco-Spanish summit in this Mediterranean port that the force proposed by France and Spain on Monday would need the approval of the U.N. Security Council which could hold an urgent meeting on Zaire later on Tuesday.

"We have suggested sending a force to ensure security... which should be decided upon by the Security Council and could be as soon as possible replaced by an African force with U.S. and European backing," Chirac said.

He said Paris and Washington had started consultations on the force to help ensure that aid gets through to more than a million refugees. The French say it should include U.S., European and African troops.
Chirac said he had requested an urgent meeting of the U.N. Security Council to discuss the plight of refugees caught in fighting between Zairean troops and Rwanda-backed Tutsi rebels.
Chirac said the meeting, also called by Germany, could take place in New York later on Tuesday.
He said ailing Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, who is now convalescing in France before flying home to Zaire, had a central role to play in solving the conflict.

"It is quite obvious that the international community cannot ignore that he is the man best-placed to represent Zaire and find a solution to this problem as far as Zaire is concerned," Chirac, flanked by Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar, said.
Mobutu, 66, arrived at his French Riviera villa near Nice on Monday from Switzerland where he was being treated for prostate cancer. He is expected to fly to Zaire in a few days.

Chirac said he believed that Zairean Prime Minister Kengo Wa Dondo would attend Tuesday's meeting of east and central African leaders in Nairobi on the situation in Zaire. Kenya has said he would not attend.
